MINUTES
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE
  AUGUST 18, 2020

1.  CHAIR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm.

2.  ROLL CALL

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Zerunyan, Boothe, Martin, Munday, Pope,
  Vanden Bos,

  COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Combs, Scott

  STAFF PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development & Public Works
  Joanne Itagaki, Traffic Engineering Deputy
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  ALSO PRESENT:  Deputy Bouse, Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES, MARCH 3,
  2020.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
MARTIN to,

  APPROVE THE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES OF
  MARCH 3, 2020.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

NONE.

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  ROLLING HILLS ROAD BIKE LANE CONCEPT ALTERNATIVES

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki provided a presentation introducing two conceptual plans for
Rolling Hills Road bike lanes. Conceptual plan (1) would include roadway widening to
accommodate 6-foot bike lanes on both sides of Rolling Hills Road, and (2) would include the
construction of protected bike lanes (cycle track) on one side of Rolling Hills Road. This would
allow for two-way bicycle travel. The cycle track would be on the east side of Rolling Hills Road
from Palos Verdes Drive North to Rolling Hills Road (private road). It would then transition to the
west side of Rolling Hills Road to the north city limit.

Director Wahba stated that there was input received regarding the cycle track moving from the
east side to the west side at Rolling Hills Road (private road). Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki
stated that it has to do with the topography in that area. There are areas where retaining walls
would likely be needed to accommodate the cycle track layout on the east side.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN stated that State laws and mandates are working towards walkability and
bike-ability; this is the city’s attempt to show that Rolling Hills Estates is moving towards this effort.
In addition, the city would be able to apply for available grants to fund walkability and bike-ability
projects.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS expressed his concern with the second option and
difficulties with traffic and visibility. Mr. Vanden Bos stated that he would prefer option one with
bike lanes on both sides of the road and commented that it may not be necessary to have
pedestrian walkways on both sides of the road.

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  1
Minutes, August 18, 2020
 COMMITTEE MEMBER MARTIN agreed and stated that he would like to see a simple design
and keep clear visibility.

COMMITTEE MEMBER BOOTHE stated that she would like to reiterate the communities concern
with having bicyclists and pedestrians cross to the other side of the street (option two).

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM stated that he is a cyclist and prefers option one. Mr. Lum stated
that it is a simple design and would likely be less costly and would be a safer alternative. He also
stated that bicyclists tend to use Palos Verdes Drive East more so than Rolling Hills Road.

COMMITTEE MUNDAY also agreed with option one and its simplicity. Mr. Munday inquired if
there are elements that could be adjusted, perhaps, the pedestrian walkway could be preserved
and the bike path could be placed elsewhere. Director Wahba stated that that the right-of-way
could accommodate both. He added that Peninsula Heritage School is on the east side of the
street and there is a connection with the middle school at St. Luke’s and there is the General
Store. It would be ideal to have a connection closer to Palos Verdes Drive North with the
pedestrian walkways on both sides of the street and then one pedestrian walkway from St. Luke’s
Church to Torrance on the west side of the street.

Ms. Govednik, Shadow Lane resident, expressed her concern with the speed in which vehicles
are travelling down this road, particularly after 8 pm and in the morning when people are late for
work. She expressed her concern with having pedestrians cross from one side of the street to the
other. She commented that she prefers option one and stated that there is more room available
to construct on the west side. She stated that her primary concern is that not many bicyclists use
this road and not many pedestrians use the road except for children during the school year. Most
children go to Kelly’s Corner to catch the bus and she stated that she did not see any
consideration for the bus system. Ms. Govednik stated that she would be in favor of a design that
shifted everything to one side of the road for safety reasons. She also would like to discuss speed
bumps.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN thanked Ms.Govednik for her comments and encouraged her to contact staff
regarding traffic calming solutions.

COMMITTEE VANDEN BOS made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE LUM to,

  DIRECT STAFF TO MOVE FORWARD WITH CONCEPTUAL PLAN OPTION ONE AND
  WORK WITH THE TRAFFIC ENGINEERING DEPUTY TO VERIFY THAT THIS WILL BE
  SUFFICIENT FOR A GRANT PROPOSAL. OTHERWISE, BRING IT BACK TO THE
  COMMITTEE FOR DISCUSSION.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

B.  DAPPLEGRAY LANES PROPERTY OWNERS ASSOCIATION (DLPOA) - TRAFFIC
  CALMING REQUEST

Director Wahba provided a brief history on requests in various neighborhoods regarding speed
bumps. A vote of fifty plus one, initiated by the homeowner’s association, is required in order to
approve a speed bump installation. There are also many factors to consider when installing speed
bumps, but the benefit is to slow traffic. Director Wahba stated that there are already three speed
bumps in the Dapplegray Neighborhood on Dapplegray Lane and it appears there is a desire to
install more.

Babak Farrokh-Siar, DLPOA President, stated that he has support from the community for speed
bumps or other methods to slow vehicles down in the neighborhood. There is a concern with
delivery trucks and other vehicles speed travelling through the neighborhood. Mr. Farrokh-Siar
stated that there are a lot of families with children, as well as horses and peacocks in the area
and expressed safety concerns.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN stated that three speed bumps were installed on Dapplegray Lane and
requested input on the feasibility to add more or other measures that may help.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki stated that there may be opportunity for one or two speed
bumps on Dapplegray Lane. Ms. Itagaki suggested that there may be an opportunity to add edge
lines to provide a safety path for pedestrians as well as a narrowing of the street. Motorists tend

Traffic and Safety Committee Meeting  2
Minutes, August 18, 2020
 to slow down when driving through a narrow street. Another suggestion is a “choker” at an
intersection, which reduces the pedestrian crossing distance and crossing time that a pedestrian
is in the street and creates a narrowing affect.

Traffic Engineering Deputy Itagaki suggested that if this moves forward, part of the traffic study
would be to take speed data in order to quantify the actual speed of the vehicles.

Director Wahba stated that the streets in the Dapplegray POA are narrow to begin with and there
are built-in drainage swells on both sides of the roadways. There is also a 12 foot wide public
right-of-way that extends from approximately the edge of pavement to the property line. This 12
foot wide area used to be where vehicles parked but properties have extended their front yards
to encroach over the public-right-of-way. There was an attempt to take back that section and it
was not met favorably. In this case, the addition of an edge line might force vehicles to park
further into the street when ideally they should be parking within the public right-of-way between
the edge of pavement and property line. Director Wahba suggested adding more signage.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS asked where the existing street bumps are located.
CHAIR ZERUNYAN responded that one is located in front of 26 Dapplegray Lane, the other two
are approximately in front of 40 Dapplegray Lane and 80 Dapplegray Lane. There are no speed
bumps on Sorrel or Buckskin. COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS asked if Sorrel is a concern
since it is only about 900 ft.

Mr. Farrokh-Siar stated that there have been a couple of complaints regarding Sorrel, but there
has been concern regarding all the streets in the neighborhood. He stated that coming into the
neighborhood, there is a steep street with a stop sign that people will run through. He mentioned
that due to COVID, there is an influx of delivery trucks and other work vehicles.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN stated that the POA should work with staff to come up with various ways to
slow down traffic and look into the feasibility and location for the installation of speed bumps.

COMMITTEE MEMBER VANDEN BOS commented that he has observed that speed bumps are
effective when they are installed closer together. When they are spread out too far, then drivers
tend to slow down and speed back up and are not particularly effective.

Ms. Govednik, Shadow Lane resident, inquired about the 12-foot section of public right-of-way in
front of properties and expressed her concerns with creating a fire hazard with emergency
vehicles being able to get in and out.

Mr. Farrokh-Siar stated that he is happy to work with staff on this issue and thanked the
committee.

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

NONE

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

COMMITTEE MEMBER LUM stated that he would like the committee to consider discussing
installing bike lanes on Palos Verdes Drive East from Palos Verdes Drive North to the city
boundary.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN stated that it would be a very short stretch of bike lane since most of Palos
Verdes Drive East south of Palos Verdes Drive North is in the City of Rancho Palos Verdes.

CHAIR ZERUNYAN added that there is a major project underway at the corner of Palos Verdes
Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East to accommodate a nature center. The project will include
updating that section of roadway and a bike lane may be very feasible.

Director Wahba stated that there is a plan to add bike lanes on Palos Verdes Drive East from the
city limits at Rancho Palos Verdes to Lomita. There is also a plan to provide better pedestrian
linkages.
